newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty edges higher, waits for NBP action.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty edges higher, waits for NBP action.

text.p: The Polish zloty slowly inched up against the basket of currencies in early Wednesday trade and players expected the National Bank of Poland (NBP) to intervene against the local currency later today.

"If the zloty strenghtens past 1.5 percent from parity the NBP will most likely intervene...and the zloty is probably headed for higher levels today," said Malgorzata Sawicka, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers said the market's recent pro-zloty sentiment as well as foreign entry prospects at today's fixed bond auction would give the zloty a boost on Wednesday.
At 0855 GMT the zloty was at 1.54/1.51 percent from parity, above the 1.5 percent resistance level and stronger than 1.56/1.46 percent at 0705 GMT.
It was at 3.2270/80 to the dollar against opening's 3.2260/90 and at 1.8628/33 to the mark against 1.8625/45.

Late on Tuesday, Standard & Poor's affirmed Poland's BBB- long-term foreign currency rating and its A- long-term local currency rating, while reviving the outlook to positive from stable on both ratings.
It also affirmed the A-1 short-term local currency rating and assigned the A-3 short-term foreign currency rating.

"The ratings could be better but these results fall within market expectations. It does not bode ill for the zloty because S & P's outlook has improved," said Witold Wozniak, dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA. "Upward pressure on the zloty may even increase slightly on the rating update," he added.
One-day rates stabilised around 22.5 percent on Wednesday after the central bank refrained from staging any drainages.
At 0910 GMT overnight rates were at 22.30/22.50 percent, donw from 22.40/22.65 at opening and tomorrow/next were at 22.40/22.50 percent against Tuesday's close at 22.30/22.60.
